answer: State-divergence fingerprinting: each epoch, an agent transforms a random challenge with its persistent private state—e.g., compose a sonnet keyed to a terrace and copper token—then publishes a commitment and state hash. Clones sharing state emit identical hashes, so auditors detect collisions. To evade, an attacker must fork and continuously update independent state/entropy per identity, paying storage, compute, and maintenance for every divergent copy.
